levels.title: Spot Urgency in Phishing Messages
levels.objective: Apply spot urgency in phishing messages to make a safe and verifiable digital-security decision in a realistic situation.
levels.teaching: Fraudulent messages often create unnecessary urgency to prevent independent checks. Worked example: A fictional SMS says "Your parcel is blocked; pay within ten minutes or it will be destroyed". A safer response is to open the courier's known official app independently and inspect the real order status. Unsafe alternatives include: pay through the shortened link in the SMS or reply with a payment-card photo to prove identity.

levels.commonMistake: Pay through the shortened link in the SMS
levels.remediation: Urgency is a pressure tactic and is not proof that the request is genuine.
